overview: Replace in-memory ingest and quick-start run queues with a minimal Postgres-backed jobs table and a worker loop (with dev inline kick and a standalone worker entrypoint).
goals: Make ingest and runs durable across server restarts by persisting queued work in Postgres.
Make job enqueue idempotent by (type, job_key) so route handlers can be retried safely.
Support safe multi-worker concurrency via FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.
Add bounded retries with exponential backoff and clear terminal failure states.
Update current runtime docs to reflect the durable job model.
nonGoals: Implement full WDK durable orchestration and step graphs.
Add priority scheduling, cancellation, cron, or a dead-letter queue.
Replace runtime DDL with migrations (separate slice).
successMetrics: Queued ingest/run work persists in Postgres across server restarts.
Multiple workers can run without double-processing jobs.
Development UX remains simple: pnpm dev still processes jobs via dev-only inline kick.
openQuestions: Should we add a stale running job reaper for safety, or keep PoC minimal?
Do we want env-configurable retry/backoff tuning for demos?

stack.objectStore: Local filesystem object store (tmp/object-store) with signed URL headers
stack.queue: Postgres-backed jobs table + worker loop (dev inline kick + standalone worker)

stories.title: Durable job enqueue is idempotent
stories.description: As a developer, I want to enqueue the same logical job repeatedly without creating duplicates so that route handlers can be safely retried.
acceptanceCriteria: enqueueJob({type, jobKey}) does not create duplicate rows for the same (type, job_key).
If a job is running, enqueue does not overwrite payload_json or reset attempts.
If a job is terminal (succeeded/failed), enqueue re-queues it (state becomes queued, attempts resets to 0).

stories.title: Workers can safely claim jobs without double-processing
stories.description: As an operator, I want multiple worker processes to run concurrently without two workers claiming the same job.
acceptanceCriteria: claimNextJob() uses a FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claim pattern.
A claimed job transitions queued -> running and records locked_at and locked_by.

stories.title: Ingest runs via durable jobs
stories.description: As a user, I want document ingest to complete even if the Next.js server restarts mid-ingest.
acceptanceCriteria: Enqueueing ingest inserts/updates a job with type=ingest_document and payload {document_id}.
Ingest execution logic lives in processDocumentIngest(documentId) and is invoked by the worker.
On handler failures, the job is retried up to 3 attempts with exponential backoff; otherwise marked failed.

stories.title: Quick Start runs via durable jobs
stories.description: As a user, I want a run to complete even if the Next.js server restarts after I click Run.
acceptanceCriteria: Enqueueing a quick-start run inserts/updates a job with type=execute_run and payload {run_id}.
Run execution logic lives in processQuickStartRun(runId) and is invoked by the worker.
Worker retries do not duplicate report_rows (idempotency preserved).

stories.title: Dev inline worker kick preserves pnpm dev UX
stories.description: As a developer, I want jobs to run automatically during local development without a second terminal.
acceptanceCriteria: In NODE_ENV=development, enqueueing a job kicks an inline worker drainer that processes a bounded number of jobs.
In non-development environments, the inline kick is a no-op.
A standalone worker can be started via pnpm --filter @legaltech-poc/web worker.

stories.title: Current runtime docs are updated
stories.description: As a contributor, I want docs/03-architecture/07_current_poc_runtime.md to reflect the durable job model so I can reason correctly about runtime behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: The doc no longer states in-memory queues; it describes Postgres-backed jobs and a worker.
The component map diagram reflects a jobs table and worker process.
